what.text: This page follows refugees from Afghanistan in Iran and Pakistan combined, the countries that host the most Afghan refugees.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 1158538 Afghan refugees in Pakistan and 758339 in Iran.
From 2025, UNHCR also counts some Afghans in Iran and Pakistan as other people in need of international protection, a separate group.

why.text: Soviet forces entered Afghanistan on 27 December 1979, and UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Afghanistan in every year from 1978 to 2025.

Over that span the government's opponents in UCDP's records include the PDPA, Hizb-i Islami-yi Afghanistan and the Taleban, and UCDP also records armed conflict with the Islamic State group from 2015.
The Taliban took control of Kabul on 15 August 2021, and new arrivals in Iran and Pakistan followed.

when.text: UNHCR's figures for Iran and Pakistan rise steeply from 1980 and peak at 6314110 in 1990.
In 2002, after the fall of the Taliban government, returns from Pakistan and Iran were the largest in UNHCR's returns data.
Pakistan announced a plan in October 2023 to return foreigners without valid documents, and by the end of 2025 Iran and Pakistan together hosted 1916877 Afghan refugees.

how.text: Many Afghans in Iran and Pakistan are not counted as refugees, so these figures are not a count of every Afghan living there.
Iran's 2022 figure follows a recount, so read UNHCR's footnote before comparing 2021 with 2022.
Returns in 2025 were on the scale of 2002, mostly from Iran.
